questions.question: What does a React Native `View` become on Android?
options: An HTML div inside a WebView
Nothing until the app is published
questions.explanation: React Native creates real platform views (android.view.View on Android, UIView on iOS) rather than rendering HTML.

questions.question: Your component runs a long, heavy calculation in JavaScript. What is the likely visible effect?
options: The app ignores taps and UI updates until the JS thread is free
Nothing, because JavaScript runs on the GPU
The app automatically moves the work to a server
Only the Android version is affected
questions.explanation: Your React code runs on the single JS thread; while it is busy it can't handle events or tell the native side about UI changes.

questions.question: What is the difference between props and state?
options: Props are only for styling; state is only for text
State is passed in by a parent; props are owned by the component
Props are read-only inputs from a parent; state is data the component owns and can change, triggering a re-render
questions.explanation: Props flow down from the parent and are read-only. State belongs to the component; updating it re-renders that component.

questions.question: Why should you never judge an app's performance in a development build?
options: Development builds include debugging tooling and run noticeably slower than optimised release builds
Development builds use a different programming language
Release builds don't use JavaScript at all
questions.explanation: Dev builds add checks, warnings and debugging support. Release builds are optimised (and Hermes precompiles the bundle), so measure performance there.
